correctness.rationale: Source Algorithm 1 allows positive h and alpha; gamma_0=h gives gamma_n=h and equal couplings a=alpha/(1+alpha). Its deterministic quadratic-plus-L1 update is the stated soft threshold. Near zero the proximal input lies strictly in the dead zone, and once v=0 and x sufficiently small, x is multiplied by b on each further step. Globally the threshold subtracts a bounded perturbation of magnitude at most theta from the smooth linear update. The smooth determinant is b^2, with trace 2b+a^2(1-k); the Schur inequalities reduce to 1-b^2, a^2 k, and a^2(k_*-k) all positive, so summable powers and bounded input give all-start boundedness below k_*. An antipodal orbit forces v=-c x and, after selecting x>0 by oddness, the active threshold equation a(k-k_*)x=theta. It has the unique positive solution exactly in the supercritical regime. On the positive-sign cone x>=X and v=-cx-w, w>=0, the explicitly positive input gives x^+=-x-aw and w^+=a(k-k_*)(x-X)+(b^2+a^2(k-k_*))w. The sign-reversed cone follows by oddness. The two-dimensional displacement matrix has strictly positive entries and characteristic polynomial negative at 1. Every nonzero nonnegative displacement thus has a positive Perron projection with expanding eigenvalue >1 and its x-displacement grows exponentially. On the prescribed diagonal x_0=v_0=R, x_1=R and the negative active threshold yields v_1=(1-ak)R+theta<-cR for the stated R; ak_*-2/a=2b^2/a>0. This verifies entry with nonzero displacement and alternating divergence.
residual_risks: Uniqueness covers antipodal cycles only; the equality k=k_* is not classified. Subcritical boundedness is not subcritical global convergence. Not all supercritical diagonal starts escape.
